newsitem.title: USA: Information vendors say win ruling against Nynex unit.
newsitem.headline: Information vendors say win ruling against Nynex unit.

text.p: A group of companies that sell information services through the "976" telephone number said Wednesday a state agency law judge ruled in its favour in a case involving New York Telephone Co., a Nynex Corp. unit.

The group, which provide sports, financial news, weather, horoscope and other information, said Public Service Commission administrative law judge Frank Robinson recommended awarding the companies damages of between $40 million and $50 million.
A statement by the group said Robinson found that New York Telephone engaged in "gross negligence and wilful misconduct," including a cover-up in the legal proceedings.
A New York Telephone spokesman said the company strongly disagreed with Robinson's recommendations and comments.

The companies that issued the statement include Accurate Info Ltd., Statistical Phone Information Services and Phone Programmes Inc. Tom Butler, a spokesman for Phone Programmes, said the three are major players in the so-called "mass announcement services" business.
Through New York Telephone, the vendors sell information via brief messages at a charge of 40 cents a call. Fifty percent of the charge goes to the vendor and the other fifty percent to NY Telephone.

They complained that when New York Telephone replaced certain equipment and software in 1990, problems developed. They said many callers could not get to their programmes and instead heard busy signals or their phones went dead. They alleged they lost business as a result.

New York Telephone spokesman Steve Marcus said the company "strongly disagrees" with Robinson's recommendations and comments. He said New York Telephone will file a brief in the first week of February seeking a full Public Service Commission review of Robinson's ruling.

Marcus said Robinson's recommendations were "fundamentally flawed," adding that New York Telephone acted responsibly in putting up a digital switch to process calls to information services. The company also acted promptly to resolve any problems that arose from the installation of the new equipment, he said.
